bands.label: Lancet letter and IMA pushback
bands.summary: Over 1,150 health professionals signed a Lancet-published letter on Jun 16 demanding IMA suspension from the WMA, and the Israeli Medical Association publicly denounced the proposal days later.

bands.label: Gaza war and medical mobilization
bands.summary: The Oct 7 attack and the subsequent Gaza war drove sustained public-health and medical-professional debate over Israeli institutional responsibility and over hospital and clinician harm in Gaza.

bands.label: BDS pressure and boycott debates
bands.summary: Academic, cultural and professional boycott campaigns targeting Israeli institutions expanded through the 2010s, setting precedents and vocabulary that later medical-association proposals draw on.

frames.label: Jun 2026 Lancet letter
frames.note: This is the frame the Lancet signatories and Maktoob coverage open with. Under this start, the story is health professionals citing documented harms in Gaza and asking the World Medical Association to apply existing membership rules to the Israeli Medical Association. It reads as a profession-internal accountability question.

frames.label: Oct 2023 attack and war
frames.note: This is the frame the Israeli Medical Association and Jerusalem Post coverage open with. Under this start, the story is a wartime boycott campaign aimed at a national medical body whose country was attacked on Oct 7, with the IMA calling the proposal a weaponization of medicine. It reads as politicization of a clinical institution during active conflict.

frames.label: 2010s boycott wave
frames.note: This is the frame longtime boycott-movement observers and Forward coverage on individual targeting open with. Under this start, the story is the latest step in a longer boycott trajectory that has moved from institutions toward individuals across academia, culture and now medicine. It reads as continuity with prior BDS-era debates rather than a new event.
